text:
**Short answer:** Yes, at about $450-$500 it's a good buy if you mostly run AC appliances (camping, power tools, short outages). If weight, noise, or USB/DC use matter to you, look at its successor first.

**What it offers**
- 1,152 Wh LiFePO4 battery rated for 3,500+ cycles, 1,800 W output (2,700 W surge), and a 5-year warranty ([BLUETTI US](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)).
- Real usable capacity is about 950-1,039 Wh across six independent tests, or 82-90% of the rated capacity ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)). PCWorld called its AC efficiency class-leading ([PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html)).
- Fast recharging: 0-80% in about 45 minutes in Turbo mode ([BLUETTI US](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)).

**Drawbacks**
- **Weight:** about 35-37 lb. OutdoorGearLab scored its power-to-weight ratio poorly and found the fan noisy ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180)).
- **Small loads:** at a roughly 34 W load, one tester got only 620 Wh (54%). That matters for a CPAP or an overnight fridge ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **DC and USB:** PCWorld measured only 71% DC efficiency, and the four USB-A ports are slow ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)).
- **Heat:** output drops to 1,500 W between 95°F and 104°F. One app setting (Grid Enhancement) can also stop the backup function from working ([Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Expansion:** sources disagree. OutdoorGearLab says it's expansion capable, while Dealectric says it can only be topped up from a B80/B230/B300 battery in Power Bank Mode. Check this if expansion matters to you.

**The newer option:** OutdoorGearLab says BLUETTI's successor, the Elite 100 v2, is smaller and lighter (25 lb), quieter, and faster charging, with a lower street price. Its capacity is a bit lower at 1,024 Wh. They consider it the better product ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180)). I didn't get a purchase link for it in these results.

**Price:** The official store lists it at $499. Some sources have seen promotions at $399-$449, with inconsistent stock ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)). I'd pay $450 or less. Around $500, the lighter newer models and rivals look better, and Best Batteries notes it costs more than some similar-capacity competitors.

**Where to buy:** [BLUETTI US, AC180 at $499](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603). It has a 30-day price-match guarantee. Dealectric, an affiliate site, reports that code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off in BLUETTI's cart on Oct 21 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180)). The checkout has the final say on whether it applies.
